He Bought a BMW M3 CS and Parked It, Then Listed It for Sale a Month Later
43 photos
Photo: Cars and Bids
Sometimes it's incompatibility. Other times, it's about some other car. And other times it is just about cashing in. Those are some of the reasons why people end up listing for sale the car that they just bought. This is one of those stories. The original owner bought this 2027 BMW M3 CS Handschalter in October 2026. A month later, it is already for sale.
This BMW checks all the right boxes. Well, of course, if you like the “beaver teeth.” I, for one, must admit that it is starting to grow on me, especially when it comes with the red border trim and black-and-red “M3 CS” badging. Right, busted, guilty pleasure! Aside from that, there is really nothing to point out as an obvious flaw on this M3.
It is an M3 CS, which stands for Competition Sport, but you might as well pretend it stands for "Constant Sliding," because that is exactly what happens in the millisecond you turn off traction control on a damp track. Whatever you go for, this car sure sounds like fun from bumper to bumper.
Then, just look at it. It is finished in the showstopping Isle of Man Green Metallic, which looks just as good as Twilight Purple Pearl, over an Anthracite interior with M Carbon bucket seats and Merino leather upholstery. The car rides on lightweight forged Style 827M wheels, measuring 19 inches up front and 20 inches out back.
Photo: Cars and Bids This BMW M3 CS has the wheels finished in matte black, but the other option would have been matte gold bronze, which would have surely been a bit too much. The hood features two distinct recessed stripes left unpainted to show off the exposed carbon weave underneath because this car comes with tons (it’s a metaphor, not actual tons!) of carbon fiber.
The car comes with the Handschalter designation, which is German for "hand shifter." I told you it checks all the right boxes. That six-speed manual transmission puts down what the twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter straight-six pushes out through the rear wheels. Told you it’s built in the name of fun!
That would be 473 horsepower (480 metric horsepower) and 406 pound-feet (550 Newton meters) of torque, which is enough to make it rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 4.1 seconds and top out at 180 mph (290 kph) when the M Driver's Package is involved. Every single M3 CS Handschalter leaves the factory with the package.
However, the original owner didn’t enjoy much of that performance. He listed the 2027 BMW M3 CS Handschalter for sale with just 68 miles (109 kilometers) on the clock, which is basically delivery mileage and driving around the block a couple of times.
Photo: Cars and Bids The manual BMW M3 CS is so cool that even Doug DeMuro, who reviewed it, said he wanted it. " I considered calling @Cargovoyage and telling him that I was keeping it, " he wrote in the comments section of the listing.
" Go for it, Doug! " the seller replied. However, DeMuro has just bought a 2006 Ford GT Heritage Edition for an undisclosed price, soon after selling his Midnight Blue 2005 Ford GT “never liked the color” non-Heritage Edition for $540,000, so he might not be in the market for another car just yet.
The still-new manual BMW is part of a special production run rolled out in very limited numbers, exclusive to North America . BMW hasn't indicated the exact number of units to be produced, but dealer allocation reports indicate a production of roughly 640 to 740 units.
It comes with carbon fiber components all over, such as carbon ceramic brakes and a carbon fiber roof panel, along with unique chassis tuning, which shaves off 75 pounds (34 kilograms) of the weight of the standard M3 in this spec.
Photo: Cars and Bids Because removing the front-axle all-wheel-drive system frees up clearance, the BMW M3 CS Handschalter with rear-wheel drive sits a quarter of an inch (6 millimeters) closer to the pavement compared to the standard M3.
The future owner is getting a brand-new car, which hasn’t even required service yet, with a gorgeous spec and no need to wait for months to have it delivered, along with two keys, the owner’s manual, the window sticker, and the wheel lock key.
The original owner paid $119,150 to drive this BMW off the showroom floor. Now, with six days to go, the most generous offer out of the 13 bids already placed is inching closer to the sticker and will most likely go way past it. Right now, it sits at $113,476 and counting.
" All that money for a car that'll get walked on by a Tesla Model 3 Performance, " someone wrote in the comments section. But the Model 3 Performance has no Isle of Man paint and definitely no manual transmission. There is no comparison between the two for a real car enthusiast.
This purchase and sale after just one month of ownership is starting to look every inch like a tutorial about cashing in. However, surprisingly, nobody asked the seller why he is selling so fast.
